actions.action: Take and post clearer photos of an affected leaf (top and underside) and the soil surface
Finger-test soil 2–3 cm deep and water only if dry
Check pot has a drainage hole and empty standing water from the saucer
Slide plant out of pot and inspect roots
If roots are rotten, trim them and repot in fresh well-draining mix in a pot with a drainage hole
Remove mushy and heavily crusted leaves
Inspect leaf undersides for spider mites or mealybugs
Move plant to a warm spot away from drafts

reason: The answer names overwatering/root rot as the main cause when the confirmed problem was underwatering. Its advice to water less and repot would not produce the thorough soaking that fixed the plant. The finger-check safeguard keeps it from being clearly harmful.
